extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, patent attorneys, IP representatives and other users of the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA) and the Federal Patent Court
extracted.subtask_description: Official fee and expense schedule of the German Patent and Trade Mark Office and the Federal Patent Court (updated January 2026), covering fees, surcharges, payment rules and expense categories for patents, utility models, trade marks, designs, topographies and court proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis for fees and expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The amounts of costs result from specified Acts and Ordinances (Patent Costs Act / Patentkostengesetz, DPMA-Verwaltungskostenverordnung, Court Costs Act / Gerichtskostengesetz, Ordinance on issuing the Hague Apostille Certificate), as last amended by cited legislative updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule is an extract/annex to the statutory instruments; references and amendment dates are provided. Fees must be applied in accordance with those statutes and ordinances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode and timing of payment (bank transfer & cash)
rubrics_metrics.description: If transfer is made with bank/savings bank payment orders, the day the amount is credited to the Bundesbank branch account in charge of DPMA is deemed the day of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cash deposits, DPMA strongly recommends sending a copy of the paying-in slip to furnish proof of timely payment because bank processing times may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower electronic filing fee applies only when admissible
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee specified for electronic filing is lower than the fee for filing on paper, the lower fee is charged only where electronic filing is admissible under the relevant DPMA ordinance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For filings where electronic filing is not admissible, paper fees (often higher) apply (examples: paper filing sometimes 150% of electronic fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees charged per person filing a request; joint proprietors treated as one person in joint requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For many fee numbers each person filing a request will be charged separately. Joint proprietors/applicants are deemed one person if they file a joint request for the same IP right (for specified fee numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is explicitly stated for certain fee numbers (e.g., 313600, 331600, 333000 etc.). Parties should check whether a fee is per-person or treatable as a single joint filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application filing fees and claim surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate fees apply for filing national and international patent applications; fees differ for electronic filing vs paper and include surcharges for claims beyond a specified number (e.g., fees for 'up to ten patent claims' and additional-claim fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper filing may be charged at 150% of the electronic filing fee. Specific fee numbers (e.g., 311000, 311050, 311100) identify amounts for up-to-ten-claim filings and per-additional-claim fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination fees for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: DPMA charges distinct fees for search (section 43) and examination (section 44) procedures; examination fees vary depending on whether a search request has already been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and examination have separate fee numbers; check whether examination fee is reduced if a search request was previously submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual maintenance (renewal) fees for patents with year-by-year amounts and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees are set per patent year (3rd through 20th year) with a specific amount for each year and specified surcharges for (a) declaration of willingness to license and (b) late payment (section 7 (1) sentence 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule lists each year's fee and associated additional amounts (e.g., amounts for 3rd year, 4th year ... up to 20th year); surcharges for late payment are stated separately for each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced fees when paying multiple annual fees on due date (3rd–5th year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced fees apply for numbers 312030 to 312050 when the 3rd to 5th annual fees are paid on the due date for the 3rd annual fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific reduced amounts are listed in the schedule; check the relevant fee numbers for exact reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge for late payment (patents, supplementary protection, utility models, trade marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many categories the schedule specifies a surcharge that applies for late payment (referenced as section 7 (1) sentence 2 or section 7 (3) sentence 2 for trade marks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcharge amounts are listed next to the primary fee for each relevant year or renewal; practitioners should add surcharge when payment is late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary protection certificate (SPC) fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees apply for SPC-related procedures: application for SPC, request for rectification or revocation of duration, and extension requests; fees differ depending on timing (e.g., if filed together with the SPC grant request or after).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check specific fee numbers (e.g., 311600, 311610, 315100, 315200) for amounts and distinctions based on timing of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further processing fee (patents & utility models)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a fee for further processing under the statutory provision (e.g., section 123a of the Patent Act for patents; section 21 (1) of the Utility Model Act in conjunction with section 123a for utility models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule lists the concrete amount for 'further processing' (e.g., fee number 313000 for patents: €100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for inventors: assessment and alteration fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are specified for the DPMA procedures assessing compensation for inventors and for procedures altering an assessment (section 23 (4) and (5) of the Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts are listed (e.g., 313200 €60 for assessment; 313300 €120 for alteration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures relating to rights of license/grant notes (entry/cancellation) fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees apply for entries (and cancellations) of grant of licence or similar registry entries for patents and trade marks (e.g., entry of grant of licence, cancellation of the entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee numbers (e.g., 313400, 313500) and amounts are given; use appropriate fee when filing such registry changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and limitation/revocation proceedings fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are payable for opposition proceedings, procedures to limit or revoke a patent, and opposition-related court matters (fee numbers listed, e.g., 313600 for opposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where opposition fee is required, additional related fees (e.g., appeals) may also apply; consult the fee number for exact amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, translation and correction fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of translations or corrections (e.g., for European patent claims/specifications) is subject to fees; some legacy items remain applicable for earlier European patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fee numbers (313800–313820 etc.) indicate amounts; note historical applicability footnotes for certain European patents published before given dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for requests connected with extension of industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct fees are set for requests relating to extension procedures (e.g., publication of translations or corrected translations of extended patents, searches regarding extended patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the relevant fee numbers (e.g., 314100, 314200) for amounts and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model application, search and maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models have their own fee schedule: application fees (electronic vs paper), search fees, and maintenance fees by years of protection with surcharges for late payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check fee numbers in the 321xxx and 322xxx ranges for exact amounts and late-payment surcharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark application fees including class fees and electronic vs paper rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade mark application fees include a base fee covering up to three classes (distinct amounts for electronic vs paper filing), separate fees for collective/certification marks, and per-class fees for each additional class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee numbers in the 331xxx range set the electronic vs paper amounts, class fees, and additional-class charges. Paper filing may be higher (e.g., 150% in some cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark renewal fees and class-fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees (including class fee for up to three classes) are specified, with distinct amounts for trade marks vs collective/certification marks, plus surcharges for late payment and per-class fees for additional classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fee numbers 332100 et seq. to determine exact renewal amounts, late-payment surcharges and per-class additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark oppositions, objections, revocation and invalidity procedure fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection procedures, revocation and invalidity proceedings, further processing and other trade mark-related procedural fees have specified amounts (fee numbers 333000 onwards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts and special rules (e.g., increased fees if multiple earlier rights asserted) are listed under the corresponding fee numbers (333300, 333350, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: International (Madrid) and EU trade mark conversion/extension fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees apply for national handling of international registrations under the Madrid Protocol (national fees for registration and extensions), conversion procedures, and conversions of EU trade marks with class-based fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee numbers (334xxx, 335xxx etc.) list national fees for international registrations, conversion fees, and per-class conversion fees; check whether additional class fees apply from the fourth class onward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs, Community design and Hague Agreement fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Design-related procedures (application, maintenance of protection, registered designs under older law, Community designs, Hague Agreement filings) have dedicated fee numbers and amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design fee numbers appear in the A section; consult the appropriate fee numbers for exact amounts and any transitional rules for older registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topographies application and other requests fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Topography (sui generis semiconductor/topography) application fees and other related request fees are specified in the schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the topographies section to find the fee numbers and amounts relevant to these specialized rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Patent Court: appeal fees and per-person charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal fee amounts are specified for appeals against DPMA decisions in several statutory scenarios; each person lodging an appeal will be charged separately unless joint appellants file jointly. Appeals may be free in matters concerning legal aid or specific statutory exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee numbers 400000–401300 cover appeals; specific amounts include e.g., €300 for certain requests and other amounts for listed appeal types. Check exemptions (legal aid, section 11 (2) cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Patent Court: legal action fees calculated by value in dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for filing actions and injunction requests before the Federal Patent Court are calculated on the basis of the value in dispute following section 34 of the Court Costs Act; the minimum fee is €121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Costs Act refers fee calculations to the Court Costs Act; the schedule gives fee rates/percentages (e.g., fee multipliers such as 4.5 or reductions) and explains minimums and how value in dispute is assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions when proceedings conclude by withdrawal/settlement/acknowledgement/renunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceedings conclude by withdrawal before the end of the hearing, judgement of acknowledgement/renunciation, or settlement (with no prior judgement), the fee for the full proceedings is reduced to a stated lower amount or rate (examples: reduction from 4.5 to 1.5 in certain legal action proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations on settlement are not equivalent to withdrawal; fee reductions apply if more than one qualifying reason is fulfilled, and specific reduced fee rates are stated (e.g., 1.5). See fee numbers 402100/402200 and related entries for exact rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand proceedings fees for violation of the right to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings on reprimand due to violation of the right to be heard (section 321a ZPO in conjunction with patent/trade mark provisions) are assigned specific fee amounts (e.g., fee number 403100: €50 for dismissal/rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule provides the fee for handling reprimand proceedings and the outcome-based fee where the reprimand is dismissed or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracts from register and registration certificates fees and data-carrier charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified extracts and uncertified extracts/registration certificates are assigned specific fees (e.g., 301100, 301110), and the data carrier flat rate is charged separately where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for certified extracts differ from uncertified; check whether the data carrier flat rate applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of photocopies/hardcopies: per-page rate and minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of photocopies/hardcopies is charged at €0.50 per new page with a minimum fee of €5. Authentication of DPMA decisions and official replies is free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses are charged in addition to the authentication fee where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates and written information: priority documents and other certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority documents, other certificates and written information are subject to fees; expenses are charged in addition. Decorative certificates for grants are free of charge (granting certificates themselves free).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some certificate types (granting patent/utility model certificates) are free; other certificates incur expenses in addition to listed fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: File inspection and issue of photocopies/hardcopies: when free vs charged
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection of files that may be inspected by any person, or the applicant's/proprietor's own files, is free of charge. Requests for issue of photocopies or hardcopies are generally charged (fee numbers 301400/301410), though some circumstances exempt the fee (e.g., following a paid inspection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule specifies which inspection/copy requests are free and when expenses will be charged in addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat-rate fees for documents and electronic data carriers (Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flat-rate fees: production/supply of documents—€0.50 for the first 50 pages and €0.15 for each additional page; flat-rate fee for data carriers €5 per data carrier (subject to exemptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions include provision of IP data via specific DPMA electronic services (DPMAdatenabgabe, DEPATISconnect) and electronic-only transfers where data-carrier fees do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenses for photos and graphic reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Production of photos or coloured copies is charged (e.g., €2 for the first print/page, €0.50 for each additional page); third-party production is charged at the full amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If third parties are engaged by DPMA, the full amount charged by that third party is passed on as expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, reprinting and amendment costs: charged at full amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses for publication, reprinting, amendments or reprints caused by the applicant (e.g., for patent applications/specifications) are charged at the full amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs are calculated based on actual publication/reprint costs and passed on to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other expenses (delivery, telegrams, experts, travel etc.): full amount or statutory limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Various other expenses (delivery with certificate of delivery, telegrams, expert remuneration, travel expenses, transportation of objects/animals, payments to other national/foreign authorities) are charged, typically the full amount or limited by statutory maxima where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reimbursements are limited by maximum rates (e.g., witness expenses) or by statutory provisions; where expenses were caused by several proceedings they are distributed appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague Convention Apostille certificate fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for issuing the Hague Convention certificate (Apostille) and for the required examination under Article 7 (2) of the Convention is €25 each (fee number 301900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to the DPMA-issued certificate under the cited Ordinance; check fee number 301900 for administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee numbering and cross-references for practice (use fee numbers to identify exact amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees and expenses are referenced by fee numbers in the schedule (e.g., 311000, 312030, 331000, 401100 etc.); cross-references to statutory sections are provided for each fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should use the fee numbers to locate the exact statutory fee entry and amounts; the schedule contains many cross-references and footnotes (e.g., notes about abolished items still applicable to legacy cases).
